YouTube title seed: What's Hiding Inside Some Smoke Alarms?
YouTube description seed: That alarm on your ceiling has a secret. Guess what it is. #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: Ionization smoke alarms ionize air in a small chamber so a small current flows; smoke reduces the current and triggers the alarm.
The later surprise: The air is ionized by a tiny amount of radioactive americium-241, and the dose in normal use is very small.
The very first frame shows a white smoke alarm on a ceiling as a wisp of smoke drifts toward it. Nothing in the first second gives the answer away.
Hook test: A (statement) = "Some smoke alarms never see the smoke at all."; B (question) = "How do some smoke alarms sense smoke?".
Fact boundaries: Only ionization alarms; photoelectric ones work differently. Never suggest opening an alarm. Scenes 1-3 do not name americium. The main reveal lands in scene 4.

facts.statement: Ionization smoke detectors ionize the air in a small chamber so a small current flows; smoke reduces the current and sets off the alarm.
The air in an ionization smoke detector's chamber is ionized by a tiny amount of radioactive americium-241.
The radiation dose from an ionization smoke detector in normal use is very small.

factBoundaries: Only ionization alarms; photoelectric ones work differently.

lockedVoiceover: Some smoke alarms never see the smoke at all.
Inside this type is a tiny chamber of charged air.
A small current flows. Smoke blocks it, and the alarm sounds.
What charges it? A speck of americium, with a very small dose.
So that speck is why some smoke alarms...
